Samira / Jordan,

Thanks for sharing the benchmark CSV and the description of the clinical summarization pipeline. Quick recap: your workload is memory-first (large KV caches from ~30k token patient histories, many mid-length responses), bursty during clinic hours, and you have a strict data isolation requirement so Dedicated is the right path.

High-level ask from our side: we want to propose a SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) that balances memory headroom for long contexts against predictable unit cost for steady throughput. Attached is the CSV you sent (optihealth_benchmark_results.csv) and an initial question set.

Immediate questions that will change the SKU mix:
- 95th percentile context length and percent of requests that exceed 8k tokens
- Desired p95 latency SLO (ms per user-visible response)
- Target steady QPS vs burst QPS during clinic windows

I'm looping in Dev (cc) to add raw memory/slot tradeoffs and Jasmine for ops/runbook considerations.

Proposed next step: we'll produce two options by tomorrow afternoon — (A) Performance-first: small number of H100-heavy slots with large KV headroom, and (B) Cost-priority: A100/L4 dominated with a fallthrough to H100 for large contexts. Please confirm budget guidance and PO timing so we can include contract-level capacity commitment options.

Thanks,

Please confirm budget guidance and PO timing so we can include contract-level capacity commitment options.

Thanks, Neha — below are the concrete hardware-level tradeoffs and a starting sizing model (I attached a short appendix with formulas).

Quick kernel / hardware notes:
- H100 80GB (HBM3) gives the largest KV cache per GPU and best sustained perf for long-context models. Ideal when >15% of requests need >12k tokens.
- A100 80GB is still very capable and cheaper than H100 for sustained parallel throughput; A100 40GB variants require more aggressive KV eviction/tiling for very long contexts.
- L4 (48GB) is a cost-efficient tensor RT-optimized option for short-to-medium contexts and heavy quantization; memory limited for large persistent KV caches.

Raw numbers (order-of-magnitude, derived from your CSV and our perf profiles):
- Model: 30B family, QKV + KV cache hits typical.
- Average p50 req: 3.2k tokens; p95 req: 14.8k tokens (from your CSV).
- Effective KV memory per concurrent session (p95): ~12–18 GB (depending on tokenization and embeddings).

Sizing heuristics (pilot -> steady):
- Pilot (cost-conscious): 1 x H100(80GB) + 4 x A100(80GB) OR 8 x L4(48GB) as burst nodes. Rationale: H100 acts as fallback/canonical for >8k contexts; A100s handle steady-state medium-length requests. L4s are cheaper for quantized short contexts but require careful routing.
- Production (latency focused, 100 QPS steady, 25% burst): 4 x H100 + 8 x A100 + 20 x L4. This mix gives: KV headroom for 40 concurrent long-context sessions on H100s, A100s covering majority of steady throughput, and L4s for low-cost parallelism.

Cost signals and fallthroughs:
- Autoscale policy: prefer horizontal scale on A100/L4 first (cheaper tokens) and reserve H100 capacity for pinned long-session state and canary traffic.
- Quantization: for L4 use int8/llm.int8 where model accuracy allows (gives 2–3x throughput gain). For H100/A100 keep fp16 or bf16 for fidelity.

Attachment: sku-fit-appendix.pdf (calcs, per-GPU KV headroom table, token/sec estimates)

I'll prod a short per-GPU capacity table into the appendix with exact token/sec numbers and cost per token using your projected QPS.

On Thu, Sep 16, 2026 at 10:05, dev_patel wrote:
> Pilot (cost-conscious): 1 x H100(80GB) + 4 x A100(80GB) OR 8 x L4(48GB) as burst nodes.

Adding ops/runbook and SLO implications:

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: start with 1 H100 (pinned), 2 A100 (steady), 4 L4 (burst) — route 5% of traffic (long-context flagged) to H100. Monitor p95 latency and model quality delta for quantized L4 routes.
- KV caching: enable prefix and patient-session sticky routing so we keep KV warm on H100 for active sessions. Drop to A100/L4 only when session is cold or cost policy triggers.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback chain: L4 -> A100 -> H100 (when length or quality triggers). Keep tracing tags to measure cross-GPU quality drift.
- Alerting: p95 latency > target OR model output regression on eval prompts should trigger immediate capacity shift and 1:1 page to infra oncall.

Minimal pilot config (ops-safe, cost-aware):
- 1 x H100(80GB) (pinned, holds hot KV)
- 4 x A100(80GB) (steady throughput)
- 6 x L4(48GB) (burst/low-cost parallelism)
- Autoscale buffer: spare 10% cores on A100/L4 for burst absorb

Estimate: This gives you runway for 25–40 concurrent long-context sessions with p95 latency in the 600–900ms range for most queries (specific depends on final model selection and batch config). We can tighten with model quantization and batching knobs.

Operational deliverables I can own for pilot: routing policy, rollout steps, tracing dashboard, and a short playbook for swap-to-H100 in case of quality regression.

-Jasmine

Samira — thanks for the budget constraint. We ran quick cost modelling against your usage profile and the pilot constraint ($45k/mo). Two compact options that aim to stay under budget (estimates include reserved monthly infra + basic support):

Option 1 (Hybrid minimal, safer quality):
- 1 x H100(80GB) (pinned) — holds hot KV and handles long-context overflow
- 3 x A100(80GB) (steady) — main throughput
- 4 x L4(48GB) (burst) — cheap parallel short-context throughput
Estimated monthly infra + support: ~$41k/mo
Pros: Keeps a clear H100 safety net for accuracy, fits budget.
Cons: Limited headroom for simultaneous very-long sessions; may need temporary quota bumps for peak clinic days.

Option 2 (Lower-flat-cost, more L4):
- 0 x H100
- 6 x A100(80GB)
- 10 x L4(48GB)
Estimated monthly infra + support: ~$37k/mo
Pros: Lower cost, more parallelism for medium contexts.
Cons: No dedicated 80GB H100 headroom; large contexts will be tiled and may see latency and occasional quality regressions. Requires stricter routing policies and an SLA waiver for long-context p95.

Recommendation: Start with Option 1 for the pilot (safer to meet your clinical-quality constraints). We'll provision a canary window where 5–10% of traffic flagged as long-context goes to the H100; routing will immediately divert if your evals detect >2% accuracy regression on L4. After week 3 of pilot we can re-evaluate and shift to Option 2 if cost discipline is the priority and the model quality margin allows it.

Next steps I can drive:
- Draft PO template and a short SOW (we have a doc link we can share)
- Prepare a one-page runbook and a 6-week success criteria checklist
- Schedule procurement sync (I can be on the call)

Doc links: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1X-opti-pilot-estimates (cost worksheets)
PO template: https://app.docusign.com/OPTI/PO-templates/2026

If you confirm Option 1, we can target a pilot kickoff within your 3-week procurement window.
